Consult Summary:
- Mary Jo, a recreational athlete training for a marathon, presents with a 2-week history of right knee pain with clicking reproduced by running and gym activity; clinician advised conservative management (ice, reduce running), physiotherapy referral, and prescription of a stronger NSAID (to be sent to pharmacy).

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Right knee pain with audible/subjective clicking; intermittent tingling in right toes once after a run.
- Timeline:
  - Symptoms began approximately 2 weeks ago.
  - Started longer runs about 1 month ago while training for a marathon (event planned in June).
  - Pain typically begins ~20 minutes into a run (~2.5–3 miles); first episode had mild swelling that improved with ice; currently not swollen at rest and not painful at time of consult.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Exacerbated by longer runs and certain gym movements (flexion/extension during abdominal exercises).
  - Improved with ice; patient advised to continue ice therapy.
- Associated symptoms / review of systems:
  - One episode of tingling in right toes after a run; otherwise no persistent numbness, no colour/temperature change, no calf pain.
  - No giving-way episodes reported (patient uncertain of term; denies instability).
  - No locking, no difficulty going up/down stairs, normal walking, full range of motion as reported (able to fully flex and extend).
  - Occasional peripheral swelling noted by indentation from socks after prolonged standing.
  - No other joint swelling, no systemic symptoms (fever, malaise) reported.
- Other relevant points:
  - Prior ice-hockey fall months ago causing a large bruise; no ongoing left knee symptoms.
  - Patient expresses concern about possible ligament injury (e.g., ACL) from online reading; clinician stated diagnosis not possible by video.

Past Medical History:
- Ocular: Far-sighted; LASIK surgery performed.
- Urinary: History of a severe urinary tract infection; was evaluated in ER when kidney stones were suspected (details limited).
- General: Otherwise describes routine minor illnesses (colds).
- Medications (patient-reported):
  - Ibuprofen — patient states up to 400 mg at times (dose/route/frequency partially documented: "400 mg max" reported).
  - Aleve — patient uncertain of drug class (name documented; dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Vitamin D — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Melatonin — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Alprazolam (Xanax) — used occasionally for sleep/anxiety (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Occasional cannabis use: "smoke a joint" sometimes.
- Allergies: Not documented.

Social History:
- Exercise/activities:
  - Training for a marathon (planned in June); running up to 7–8 miles on some runs; started longer runs ~1 month ago.
  - Attends gym a few times per week; plays ice hockey.
- Substance use:
  - Occasional cannabis use (smokes a joint).
  - Alcohol and tobacco use not documented.
- Living situation: Lives at 60 Sloane Avenue, London (confirmed); privacy intact during consult.
- Occupation/financial factors: Not documented.

Family History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not provided in transcript.
- Examination findings: No formal physical examination findings documented in the consult (no objective knee exam recorded).

Investigations:
- No imaging or diagnostic tests reported or available in the transcript.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Right knee pain with clicking (onset 2 weeks; related to increased running/training)
  - Assessment/diagnosis:
    - Right-sided knee pain with clicking/crepitus temporally related to increased running; exact structural diagnosis not determined in the consult.
    - Differential possibilities discussed by clinician included overuse injury and potential cartilage/ligament pathology; definitive diagnosis not possible via video consultation.
  - Plan:
    - Conservative measures: continue ice therapy as tolerated.
    - Activity modification: reduce running intensity/distance; avoid running through pain.
    - Analgesia/anti-inflammatory: clinician offered to prescribe a "slightly stronger anti-inflammatory" to take instead of current ibuprofen; prescription to be sent to the patient's pharmacy (medication name/dose/route/frequency not documented in transcript).
    - Medication guidance: do not take the new prescription concurrently with ibuprofen; take NSAID with food.
    - Referral: arrange physiotherapy appointment for formal assessment and management (clinician to send referral).
    - If physiotherapy wait is long, clinician offered in-clinic assessment as alternative.
    - Safety-netting: return/seek urgent care if persistent swelling, heat, redness of the knee, high temperature, systemic unwellness, or if the knee locks and cannot bend or straighten.
- Issue 2: Single episode of right toe tingling after a run
  - Assessment/diagnosis:
    - Transient paresthesia reported once after a run; no ongoing sensory deficit reported.
  - Plan:
    - Monitor for recurrence or progression; review during physiotherapy/clinic assessment if persists or worsens.
- Issue 3: Patient anxiety regarding possible ligament/ACL injury
  - Assessment/diagnosis:
    - Patient expresses concern based on online information; clinician emphasized that diagnosis cannot be made remotely.
  - Plan:
    - Reassurance; recommend physiotherapy assessment and potential imaging if physio/clinician deems necessary.
    - Offer in-person clinic review if patient prefers or if symptoms worsen.

General plan items:
- Prescription: clinician to send a stronger anti-inflammatory to pharmacy (dose/route/frequency not documented in transcript).
- Referral: physiotherapy referral to be sent.
- Follow-up: return earlier if worsening symptoms or urgent signs as above; otherwise follow-up via physio/clinic as arranged.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Allergies: not documented.
  - Complete medication reconciliation: doses/routes/frequencies missing for multiple meds (Aleve, vitamin D, melatonin, Xanax, stronger NSAID to be prescribed).
  - Objective vital signs and physical examination findings (inspection, palpation, range of motion, ligamentous tests, gait) were not documented.
  - Neurovascular exam of the lower limb not documented.
  - Imaging or lab tests: none performed or reported.
  - Occupation and alcohol/tobacco use not documented.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Early in the consult the patient briefly referenced "knees" plural; later clarified symptoms are primarily in the right knee. (Conflict noted.)
  - Patient uncertain about the identity/class of "Aleve" (patient states she cannot remember drug class) — factual uncertainty about medication classification (not a clinical conflict but noted).
- Transcript quality comment:
  - Transcript is generally clear and intelligible with minimal background noise; several conversational fillers present but key clinical details are well documented.
